deck_title: Apple-Style Product Scrollytelling Architecture: Single Shared WebGL2 Scissor Canvas + IntersectionObserver LRU (c_scroll = c_0/(1+u), 1.0000x Lock) vs Naive 16-Canvas Context Exhaustion Crash

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Apple-style Product Launch Scrollytelling WebGL2 architecture evaluation (mounting a single fixed full-viewport WebGL2 canvas across 17 interactive 3D chapters, slicing each active DOM placeholder rect via gl.scissor() and gl.viewport(), and sleeping offscreen chapters via IntersectionObserver so amortized unit cost c_scroll(u) = c_0 / (1 + u) reaches 0.5000 at u = 1.0, locking C_active / C_scroll = 1.0000x with 0 context-loss crashes across all 17 chapters u in [0.000, 1.000]) versus naive per-section <canvas> instantiation (which exceeds iOS Safari 8-context and desktop Chrome 16-context hardware limits, triggering WEBGL_lose_context blank-canvas crashes and inflating GPU/rework cost by 1 + u to 1.2500x at C4, 1.5000x at C8, and 2.0000x at C16 across 16/17 chapters) and 64-frame viewport quadrature.

Using a single fixed WebGL2 canvas with gl.scissor() and gl.viewport() virtualized into DOM placeholder bounding rects (Drei <View> / custom Scissor Orchestrator)
Combining IntersectionObserver 1-screen preload and ±2-screen LRU GPU texture disposal to prevent mobile iOS Safari memory jetsam crashes
not_for: Spawning a new THREE.WebGLRenderer() and <canvas> for every scroll section (guaranteed to hit the 8/16 WebGL context limit)
Decoding 300 uncompressed 4K PNG sequence frames on the main UI thread during scroll events
Static plain-HTML documentation with zero 3D or canvas elements
